top_signal.title: What do I do about our terrible staff?
top_signal.summary: My (mid-20s F) parents have owned/operated a consignment retail business for over 20 years.   For the first 3-4 years, my dad was the one who did practically everything. Monthly accounting, opening/closing, running register most days, renting space to consignees, and buying product/pricing product/stocking our side of the stores (we have three active locations).   Over the years, he found trusted/competent managers who kept things running pretty smoothly until COVID hit. We had to temporarily shut down two of our locations for a couple of months because they were not “necessary businesses”. After reopening, our good managers slowly began quitting because they were not being paid to adequately match rapidly rising costs of living.   Since this, we have had very lackluster management and our general employees, that have been with us for YEARS, have become very comfortable doing the wrong things.   Both of my parents have grown attached to these employees and consider them friends. However, our business is going downhill - FAST. Customers are starting to leave bad reviews because the employees are rude, not helpful, and they don’t use good judgement when it comes to dealing with delicate situations with consignees or customers.   I have since taken over managing ALL THREE locations because the management we have now is, to put it mildly, incompetent.
